standard_prerequisites.name: A bounded above acyclic complex of modules with a chosen isomorphism P^i equal to Z^i direct sum Z^{i+1} has differentials given by the projection Z^i direct sum Z^{i+1} to Z^{i+1} followed by the inclusion of Z^{i+1} into Z^{i+1} direct sum Z^{i+2}
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: recorded in the proof at source lines 19373-19376 as the form of the maps P^i -> P^{i+1}
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the acyclicity of the lifted complex and the vanishing of its cohomology into the bookkeeping of the modules Z^i, which is what property (2) of the statement is applied to.

standard_prerequisites.name: The lifting property of a projective module: a map into a quotient that factors through a surjection can be lifted, and the lift can be arranged to hit a prescribed element modulo the kernel
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 19378-19382, where P^{n-1} is chosen projective and the composite P^{n-1} -> E^{n-1} -> E^n is lifted to a map P^{n-1} -> Z^n
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the new term P^{n-1} together with the differential into Z^n that extends the induction diagram one step to the left.

standard_prerequisites.name: The quotient map P -> P/IP is compatible with the given isomorphism P^i/IP^i -> E^i, so that the identification Z^n/IZ^n = Im(E^{n-1} -> E^n) holds
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the target of the lifted map with the quotient of Z^n, which is exactly the condition needed for the lifting property to apply.

core_obligations: Choose a vanishing upper bound b with E^i = 0 for i greater than b, and set up the induction hypothesis: for a given n there is a morphism of complexes from a bounded above complex P^bullet with terms in the class P to E^bullet, with all outstanding vertical maps inducing isomorphisms P^i/IP^i -> E^i, acyclic above degree n, and a diagram of the displayed shape (proof lines 19360-19372).

Extract from the induction hypothesis the decomposition P^i = Z^i direct sum Z^{i+1} whose differentials are the canonical maps, and deduce from property (2) of the statement, applied inductively, that every Z^i lies in the class P (proof lines 19373-19377).

Produce the next term: choose P^{n-1} in P together with an isomorphism P^{n-1}/IP^{n-1} -> E^{n-1}; using the identification Z^n/IZ^n = Im(E^{n-1} -> E^n) lift the composite P^{n-1} -> E^{n-1} -> E^n to a map P^{n-1} -> Z^n, and apply property (3) to conclude that this lifted map is surjective (proof lines 19378-19383).

Assemble the extension of the diagram by adding P^{n-1} and the two maps just built to the left of P^n, note that a diagram of the required shape exists for every n greater than b because the complex E vanishes there, and conclude the lemma by induction on n (proof lines 19383-19387).
proof_roadmap: Fix b with E^i = 0 for i greater than b and state the induction hypothesis: a partial lifting of E^bullet by a complex with terms in P, acyclic above degree n, with P^i/IP^i isomorphic to E^i (proof lines 19360-19372).
Split the already lifted part as P^i = Z^i direct sum Z^{i+1} and use the hypothesis that P is closed under direct summands to keep every Z^i inside P (proof lines 19373-19377).

Lift the connecting map to a surjection P^{n-1} -> Z^n using projectivity of P^{n-1} and the closure of P under surjections modulo I, extending the diagram one step to the left (proof lines 19378-19383).
Start the induction above the vanishing bound b and iterate downwards to obtain the required bounded above acyclic complex (proof lines 19383-19387).
difficulty_reason: The statement fixes a ring R, an ideal I, a class of R-modules closed under direct summands and stable under maps that are surjective modulo I, and asks that every bounded above acyclic complex whose terms are of the form P over IP with P in the class be lifted to a bounded above acyclic complex with terms in the class (statement lines 19342-19357). The proof is a downward induction on the degree under a vanishing bound: at each step the already lifted part is split as P^i = Z^i direct sum Z^{i+1} so that closure under summands keeps the cycles inside the class, and the next term is built from the projectivity of P^{n-1} together with the identification Z^n/IZ^n = Im(E^{n-1} -> E^n), after which property (3) upgrades the lifted map to a surjection (proof lines 19373-19383). What is not routine is maintaining three properties at once through the induction, namely the isomorphism modulo I, acyclicity in all degrees above the running index, and membership of every cycle in the class, which is why the two closure hypotheses are needed in exactly this form.
